summary: This is a Product class that represents a basic product with a name and price. It uses a constructor to initialize these values and provides getter and setter methods to read and modify them. The class enforces type safety by declaring that name must be a string and price must be a float.

explanations.3: This declares the namespace, which is a way to organize code and avoid naming conflicts—think of it as putting this class in a folder called 'Cavo'.
explanations.7: The 'private' keyword means this property can only be accessed from inside this class; code outside the class can't directly read or change it without using the getter and setter methods.
explanations.10: The constructor is a special method that runs automatically when you create a new Product object; the '=' signs set default values so you don't have to provide arguments if you don't want to.
explanations.20: The 'void' return type means this method doesn't return anything—it just performs an action (setting the name) and then stops.
explanations.24: The ': float' is a return type declaration that guarantees this method will always return a number, not a string or something else.
